why: Walk each concentric layer clockwise with four boundaries (the spiral walk), collect its values, sort, and write them back along the same path. The single-row and single-column layers are the bookkeeping trap.
hints: Write a function that returns the list of (r, c) cells of layer k in clockwise order.
Layer k spans rows top..bottom and columns left..right. Walk top row, right column, then the bottom row only if top < bottom, and the left column only if left < right.
For each layer: cells = path(k); vals = sorted(matrix[r][c] for r, c in cells); write vals back along cells. O(R*C log(R*C)).
pitfalls: A one-row or one-column layer must not visit a cell twice.
The number of layers is (min(rows, cols) + 1) // 2.
Write back along the same clockwise path you read from.
